chunks: Yaqub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When the Muhrim (person in Hajj/Umrah state) catches game by mistake, upon him is the Kaffarah (expiation). If he catches it a second time by mistake, upon him is the Kaffarah always, if it is by mistake. If he catches it intentionally, upon him is the Kaffarah. If he catches it a second time intentionally, he is among those from whom Allah takes vengeance, and there is no Kaffarah upon him.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a pilgrim catching game by mistake versus intentionally?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar clarifies the jurisprudence of hunting for a pilgrim (Muhrim), distinguishing between accidental and intentional catches. While expiation (kaffarah) is mandated for both the first accidental and first intentional catch, a second intentional catch exempts the pilgrim from further expiation, marking them as a recipient of Allah's direct vengeance (man yantaghimu Allahu minhu). This ruling highlights the shift from compensatory justice to divine retribution in cases of persistent deliberate violation.
